Reviewed all twelve steps and actual suppliers. The reader rowwise likelihood extension avoids -infinity on zero-weight rows; C1 regularity suffices for bounded derivatives and a Lipschitz square-root variance along nearest-CAID segments. Reachable output positivity and Vmin>0 give uniform local variance/third-moment bounds; t(log t)^2 controls global variance. Decoder-region testing split gives CDF <=epsilon+exp(-gamma); uniform Berry–Esseen and positive Gaussian density permit local quantile inversion. For epsilon<1/2 the negative quantile selects Vmin, and the quadratic deficit absorbs the O(sqrt(n)d) variance correction. Far types have a strict capacity gap (an empty far set needs no bound). DT at a minimum-dispersion CAID gives epsilon-1/sqrt(n) achievability; explicit message-count and type selections lose only O(log n) and retain at least one message. Output counting makes maximal code size finite. Both error criteria, C>0 implication, zero-variance summands, and integer rounding checked.
